title: Distinct Three-Letter Mirrors
statement:
Given a lowercase string s, count the different three-letter strings that read the same forwards and backwards (shape x y x) and can be picked from s as a subsequence: three positions i < j < k, not necessarily next to each other.

Each distinct string counts once, however many ways it can be picked.

examples.why: "aba", "aca" (both using the outer a's) and "bcb". "aba" can be picked twice but counts once.
"xyx", "xxx" and "yxy". Counting every way to pick positions would give far more.
No letter appears twice, so no outer pair exists.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: A mirror x y x is decided by its outer letter x and its middle letter y. How many outer letters are there?
For a fixed outer letter, which pair of positions gives the most room for the middle?
Use the first and the last occurrence of x. Every distinct letter strictly between them is a possible middle. Sum that over the 26 letters.

explain.intuition:
There are only 26 × 26 possible mirrors, so count candidates by their two letters, not by positions. For outer letter x, using its first and last occurrence leaves the widest gap between them. Any middle letter that fits under some other pair of xs also fits under this widest pair.

So for each letter, collect the set of distinct letters strictly between its first and last occurrence. The set's size is how many mirrors start and end with that letter. That is at most 26 passes over the string, or one pass if you use prefix counts.
steps: Record first[c] and last[c] for every letter in one pass.
For each letter c with last[c] − first[c] ≥ 2, put every character of s[first[c]+1 .. last[c]−1] into a set.
Add the set's size to the answer.
pitfalls: Counting every choice of positions instead of distinct strings. "xyxyx" has many ways to pick "xyx" but it counts once.
Forgetting that the middle may equal the outer letter: "aaa" is a valid mirror.
Including the outer positions themselves in the middle range. With "aab" the two a's are adjacent and leave no room.

solutions.title: Every triple of positions
solutions.idea: Try all i < j < k with s[i] = s[k] and put the resulting strings in a set.

solutions.title: First and last occurrence
solutions.idea: For each outer letter, count distinct letters strictly between its first and last occurrence.

followups: Answer it in a single pass with prefix letter counts instead of 26 scans.
Count distinct palindromic subsequences of length 4 (shape x y y x).
